stage1.impression: A night shopfront seen square-on through a blackened-steel frame, with a warm, hazy room behind it. It reads as a clean architectural render, not a photograph: the EARF letters are flat opaque grey vinyl, the lightbox is an even beige screen with a cartoonish dancer cut-out, the glass reflects nothing of the street, and the lower half of the window is a wall of fir slats. The one coloured object, the Ember speaker, shows only as two washed-out pink blobs behind chairs at the far end, so there is no hero.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker reads at a glance through a clear pane: silhouette above the chairs, saturated red, light through its acrylic
The window glass behaves like glass: faint reflections of the street lamps and the kerb, with darker reflections over the dark steel
The frosted name reads as acid-etched glass (translucent, warm from the room behind, bright edges), not opaque grey vinyl
The lightbox glows unevenly from behind, with falloff, and the dancer is fogged into the diffusion rather than printed on it
The far end holds detail: the back wall and screens are not near-white, the haze does not flatten the record wall
Some sign of life seen from the kerb (a figure at the bar, glasses on the sill, a coat)
Full-resolution delivery (this proof is 720 x 480) with no denoiser smear on the record wall

defects.what: Ember speaker (left) shows only as a pale pink patch behind a chair (r231 g177 b162): desaturated, cut off, unreadable
Ember speaker (right) is the same: a pale pink sliver behind the chairs
EARF letters are uniform opaque neutral grey (138/138/139, lum_range low inside the glyphs): read as vinyl signage or a 2D overlay, not frosting in the glass
Lightbox is an even flat beige field (median 108, p95 114), cooler than the room; the dancer silhouette is a soft cut-out and reads as clip art
No reflections on the glass at all: the panes read as open holes
Far end near blown (p95 218), milky with haze; the record wall is smeared by the denoiser
Pendant lamp is a bare clipped white disc (18% clipped) with no bloom or fitting detail
Patchy stamped-looking texture on the steel transom, reads as a decal, not patina
Bottom sill and wall below crushed to near black (median 4.9, crush 17.7%); the steel has no edge or sheen
Lower half of the window is a uniform fence of fir slats, evenly lit, which blocks the room and reads as a backdrop
The upper wall and fascia are flat and brown, with no material scale

changes.problem: The speaker, the frame's only colour and its hero, is hidden behind chairs and too small at the far end.

evidence.measured: two pink patches of about 20 x 20 and 30 x 20 px, both cut off at the top of the slat band at y 280

change.to: [-4.0, y aligned with one Ember speaker through the clear pane, 1.65], aimed at the speaker's mid-height, 65-75 mm, still level with true verticals

changes.expected: One Ember speaker stands clear above the chairs in a clear pane, about 8-12% of frame height, with the name and lightbox still in frame

changes.problem: The far end is nearly blown and milky, which washes the Ember from red to pink.

evidence.measured: lum_median 139.5, p95 218.5; speaker patch r231 g177 b162

change.setting: screens' images / niches' spot / haze density

changes.expected: The back wall drops to a warm mid-tone, the record wall gets edge detail, and the Ember's red saturates

changes.problem: The Ember reads pink, not red: its own light is too strong and too white against the 3700 K balance.

change.setting: area lamps on each Ember speaker
change.to: 9.0 W/m2, 2700 K, with the pinholes lowered to match

changes.expected: The cabinet reads as deep tinted red acrylic with glowing edges, not a pale pink patch

changes.problem: The frosted name is an opaque neutral-grey fill, so it reads as vinyl signage.

evidence.measured: r138 g138 b139, lum_p95 149.9: uniform and colourless against a warm room

change.setting: the window's frosted name (emission and frosted acrylic roughness)
change.to: emission 0, transmissive frosted glass (roughness about 0.35, transmission 1) so the letters pick up the warm room behind, with a slightly brighter etched edge

changes.expected: The letters are warm, translucent and lighter where the room behind is bright, with an edge highlight

changes.problem: The glass reflects nothing, so the panes read as open holes in a render.

evidence.measured: no visible reflection of the street lamps or the kerb anywhere on the panes

change.to: glass with IOR 1.52 and real Fresnel reflection, a dim opposite facade or parked car to reflect, street lamps 120 W

changes.expected: Faint street-lamp glints and soft reflections over the darker panes, without hiding the room

changes.problem: The lightbox is a flat, cool field brighter than the room, which makes it read as a projection screen.

evidence.measured: lum_median 108, p95 114 (almost no gradient), r118 b99

change.setting: screens' images (the lightbox) and frosted acrylic roughness
change.to: 0.5, with the frost rougher so the dancer fogs into the diffusion; warm the panel toward 2700 K

changes.expected: A softer, warmer glow with gentle falloff toward the frame, and a blurrier, more suggestive silhouette

changes.problem: The sill and the steel at the bottom are crushed, so the steel loses its edge and sheen.

change.to: 120 W, raking from above left; the steel's sheen slightly higher (roughness lower by about 0.1)

changes.expected: A readable sill edge and uneven brownish sheen on the blackened steel

changes.problem: Nothing alive is visible from the kerb.

evidence.measured: seen: no figure, glass or coat in the window band

change.from: glasses, menus, candles not visible from the street
change.to: a couple of rocks glasses and a candle votive on the window ledge in the frame, and a coat over a chair back in the mid-ground

changes.expected: Small highlights and a lived-in note in the foreground panes

out_of_scope.request: Lower or open the fir-slat band across the lower half of the window, which blocks the room and reads as a fence
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront and banquette are fixed room design

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember speaker larger or move it toward the window
out_of_scope.why: The speaker and the room's layout are fixed; only the camera can bring it forward
